chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Jaham, who said:

Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Muhammad, what do you say regarding a man who marries a Christian woman upon a Muslim woman?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what is my opinion in front of you?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say it, for in that you will come to learn my opinion.' I said: 'It is not allowed to marry the Christian woman upon a Muslim woman, nor a non-Muslim woman.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And why?' I said: 'Due to the Words of Allah (Exalted and Majestic): And do not marry the idolatresses until they believe.'
And do not marry the idolatresses until they believe.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what do you say regarding this Verse: And the chaste women from among those who have been Given the Book before you?' I said: 'So His Words: And do not marry the idolatresses, abrogate this Verse?' So he (peace be upon him) smiled, then was silent.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a Christian woman as a second wife if already married to a Muslim woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this dialogue from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Reza (AS) tests Al-Hasan ibn Jaham’s understanding of marital jurisprudence by asking if a man can marry a Christian woman while already married to a Muslim woman. Al-Hasan argues that the general prohibition of marrying idolatresses (Quran 2:221) abrogates the specific permission for chaste women of the Book (Quran 5:5), a view the Imam confirms through his silent smile. This exchange highlights the Shia scholarly preference for the abrogation view, emphasizing the superiority of the Muslim wife and the exclusivity of the marital bond in this context.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Jaham who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Abu Muhammad! What are you saying regarding a man who marries a Christian woman upon (as additional wife) a Muslim woman?’ I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! And what are my words in front of you<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should say it, for in that you will come to learn my<sup>asws</sup> words by it’. I said, ‘It is not allowed to marry the Christian woman upon (as additional wife) a Muslim woman nor a non-Muslim woman’.
Heasws said: ‘And why?’ I said, ‘Due to the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:221] And do not marry the idolatresses until they believe’.

Heasws said: ‘And what are you saying regarding this Verse [5:5] and the chaste women from among those who have been Given the Book before you (are lawful for you)?’ I said, ‘So Hisazwj Words [2:221] And do not marry the idolatresses Abrogate this Verse?’ So heasws smiled, then was silent’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm who has said the following:

“Abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘O abu Muhammad, what do you say about a man who marries a Jewish or a Christian woman, as a second wife, the first being a Muslim woman?’ I replied, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, my words have no meaning in your presence.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must say it; with it my words will come to light.’ I said, ‘It is not lawful to marry a Christian woman as a second wife, the first being a Muslim woman or non-Muslim woman.’
He (the Imam) asked, ‘Why is it so?’ I replied, ‘It is because of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, “You must not marry the pagan women until they become believers.’”

He (the Imam) then asked, ‘What do you say about, “Marry of the chaste woman of the followers of the book (bible) which was before you” [5:5]?’ I replied, ‘Verse 221 of Chapter 2 has cancelled verse 5:5.’ He (the Imam) smiled and remained quiet.’”
